title: Why You Can't Divide by Zero

steps.body: Division by zero is undefined: no quotient can make a nonzero total when multiplied by 0.
steps.narration: Division by zero is undefined: no quotient can make a nonzero total when multiplied by 0.

steps.body: Match division by zero to its inverse multiplication question.

widget.prompt: Which inverse equation would need a solution for 7 ÷ 0 to have a quotient?

options.feedback: Correct — but zero times every number is 0, so this equation has no solution.
This fact is true, but it does not find a number that zero can multiply to make 7.
This asks about 0 ÷ 7, where zero is the total, not the divisor.

cml.actionGoal: Use inverse multiplication to explain why 7 ÷ 0 has no quotient.
invariants: Zero times every number is 0, so 0 × ? cannot equal 7.
misconceptions: Treating zero as an ordinary divisor or copying zero as the quotient.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to be true for 7 ÷ 0 to have a quotient?

explanationVariants: Nothing multiplied by 0 gives a nonzero total.

options.label: 7; keep the original total
options.feedback: If 7 ÷ 0 were 7, then 7 × 0 would have to equal 7, but 7 × 0 = 0.

options.label: 1; use one full group
options.feedback: If 7 ÷ 0 were 1, then 1 × 0 would have to equal 7, but 1 × 0 = 0.

options.label: No quotient; no number works
options.feedback: Correct — no number multiplied by 0 gives 7, so the division has no answer.

options.label: 0; copy the zero divisor
options.feedback: If 7 ÷ 0 were 0, then 0 × 0 would have to equal 7, but 0 × 0 = 0.

steps.body: Because no number times 0 can give anything but 0, there is nothing for 7 ÷ 0 to equal.
steps.narration: Because no number times 0 can give anything but 0, there is nothing for 7 ÷ 0 to equal.

options.label: It always equals 0
options.feedback: Correct — that is why 0 cannot multiply by a number to make 12.

options.label: It always equals 1
options.feedback: Zero groups contain 0, not 1.

options.label: It always equals 12

explanationVariants: 0 ÷ 5 = 0: nothing shared among five is nothing each.
Zero AS the total is fine; zero as the divisor is not.

widget.prompt: Five equal groups contain 0 counters in all. How many counters are in each group?

commonErrors.feedback: That repeats the divisor. Sharing nothing among 5 groups leaves nothing in each.
Zero shared into 5 groups gives 0 in each group, not 1.

widget.fallbackFeedback: There is nothing to share, so each group receives nothing.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — 0 ÷ 5 = 0. Zero as the TOTAL is fine; only zero as the DIVISOR is undefined.

concept.body: To divide 5 by 0, we would need a number that makes 0 × ? = 5. No number works.
concept.narration: To divide 5 by 0, we would need a number that makes 0 × ? = 5. No number works.

check.body: Use inverse multiplication to justify the rule.
explanationVariants: Zero times every number is zero, never five.

widget.prompt: Which statement proves that 5 ÷ 0 has no quotient?

options.label: 0 × ? = 5 has no solution
options.feedback: Correct — zero times every number equals zero, so no product can be 5.

options.label: 5 × 0 = 0, so quotient is 5
options.feedback: That product is 0, not 5, so 5 cannot be the quotient.

options.label: 0 × 0 = 0, so quotient is 0
options.feedback: A quotient of 0 would require 0 × 0 = 5, which is false.

options.label: 1 × 0 = 0, so quotient is 1
options.feedback: A quotient of 1 would require 1 × 0 = 5, which is false.
